summary: Provides guidelines for personal interaction in the IETF. It is a Best Current Practice. It was replaced by RFC 7154.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3184 sets guidelines for how IETF participants work with one another in meetings and by email. It asks participants to be respectful, discuss ideas rather than attack people, think about the global Internet, and prepare for Working Group meetings; RFC 7154 later obsoleted it.

what are ietf guidelines for conduct
subtitle: Guidelines for respectful, reasoned, and prepared participation in the IETF.

tldr.problem: IETF work depends on cooperation among participants with diverse backgrounds, ideas, and communication styles.
tldr.mechanism: The memo sets guidelines to show respect, test ideas with reasoned argument, consider the global Internet, and prepare for Working Group meetings.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3184 is a Best Current Practice and was obsoleted by RFC 7154.

today: RFC 3184 is a Best Current Practice and was obsoleted by RFC 7154.

sections.title: Why the IETF Has Conduct Guidelines
sections.content: The IETF relies on cooperation among people with diverse backgrounds and communication styles. These guidelines apply as participants build consensus in person, at meetings, and through email. The memo says conflicts are resolved according to BCP 25.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF brings together people with different backgrounds to develop Internet technologies. These guidelines describe how they should work together.

sections.title: Four Principles for Participation
sections.content:
Participants should extend respect and courtesy to colleagues, including when they disagree. Since English is not the native language of many participants, native English speakers are asked to speak clearly and somewhat slowly and limit slang.

Participants should test ideas impartially using reasoned argument, not intimidation or personal attacks. They should seek solutions for the whole Internet and diverse technical and operational environments. People attending Working Group meetings should read relevant Internet-Drafts, RFCs, and email archives beforehand. Newcomers are encouraged to observe and absorb material; meetings are not intended for individual education.
sections.plainLanguage: Respect colleagues and challenge ideas with reasons, not personal attacks. Consider the needs of the whole Internet, and prepare for meetings by reading the relevant material.

sections.title: Status and Security
sections.content: RFC 3184 is a Best Current Practice that describes interaction guidelines. Its security section notes that IETF participants review protocols for security concerns and incorporate them in protocol descriptions.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo is a Best Current Practice about participant conduct. Protocol security concerns are handled in the descriptions of the protocols themselves.
